newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai Airways says rising costs hit H1 profits.
newsitem.headline: Thai Airways says rising costs hit H1 profits.

text.p: Rising fuel prices and increased personnel costs were responsible for national carrier Thai Airways International Plc's reduced six month profits, the company said on Wednesday.
Previously announced half year profits to March 31 1997 were 2.150 billion baht, against 2.462 billion for the same period a year earlier.
"Thai profits fell because of increased expenditure in two areas," the company said in a statement.
"First the rise in both jet fuel consumption and world oil prices. This caused Thai's fuel expenditure (in) the first half of the year to rise to 1.311 billion baht," the firm said.
This represented a 29.79 percent increase in fuel costs over the period, the company said.
"Second, increased Thai cost of living allowances for employees pushed up Thai's personnel expenses by 15.01 percent for the six-month period," the statement added.
Thai Airway's revenue over the period rose 5.1 percent to 42.26 billion baht from 40.210 billion a year ago.
